correctness.rationale: Niu's exact formula immediately identifies the two stabilizer cases. The sign map on the unoriented stabilizer has kernel the oriented stabilizer; a hyperelliptic involution acts as \(-I\) on integral first homology, hence trivially mod two and so preserves the Rokhlin quadratic form, giving an order-two splitting element. For odd \(p\), squared Dehn twists lie in \(H\) and realize arbitrary symplectic transvection coefficients mod \(p\); these transvections act transitively on nonzero vectors, yielding the stated orbit sizes and orbit-stabilizer lower bounds.

final_claim: For Niu's ordinary untwisted rim-surgery surface, the two possible marked extendable groups are \(E_+(a)\) and \(E_{\pm}(a)\), with \(E_{\pm}(a)\cong E_+(a)\rtimes C_2\); for every odd prime \(p\), reduction modulo \(p\) gives index lower bounds \([H:E_+(a)]\ge p^{2g}-1\) and \([H:E_{\pm}(a)]\ge(p^{2g}-1)/2\).
limitations: The congruence inequalities are lower bounds, not exact finite indices; Niu already proves the relevant subgroups have infinite index.
